meridian_meta.note: Authoritative template registry for HTML phases; keep in sync with shared.json template_files doc paths.

field-user-story-description.description: User Story description — Meridian Modern Work Item Standard: What, Why, optional Unknowns (rich HTML)

what_text.description: WHAT: clear plain-language description of the deliverable (outcome first, then technical constraints if relevant). NOT the work item title — body only. Verbs-led title lives in System.Title.

why_text.description: WHY: business/user context, risk, opportunity; assumptions stated in prose (no separate assumptions table). Quote stakeholder feedback when sourced from tickets or conversations.

unknowns.description: UNKNOWNS: open questions (one string per question); include who can answer in the string when known. Omit entirely or leave items empty when there are no unknowns.

field-user-story-acceptance-criteria.description: DONE WHEN — plain-English testable outcomes (optional group labels per row; Meridian Modern Work Item Standard)

done_when_items.description: Each block is one assertion. Set group_label when starting a new category (e.g. Expected behavior, Error handling, Boundaries); leave group_label empty for additional lines under the same category. Use plain assertions, not Given/When/Then labels.

group_label.description: Optional category label for this line (repeat only on first line of a category)

assertion.description: One testable outcome: specific, observable, falsifiable (condition → outcome → details as one sentence)

field-technical-description.description: Technical User Story description — Meridian Modern Work Item Standard: What (system change), Why (business/system justification), optional Unknowns

what_text.description: WHAT: the technical deliverable — system behavior, interface, integration, or platform change in plain language first, then precision (APIs, limits, components) as needed. NOT the work item title.

why_text.description: WHY: quantified or explicit business/system justification; risks; assumptions in prose. Boundaries and NFRs that read like finish-line checks may belong in DONE WHEN instead.

unknowns.description: UNKNOWNS: technical or product questions (one string each). Omit or leave empty when none.

field-technical-acceptance-criteria.description: DONE WHEN — technical plain-English measurable outcomes (same slot shape as functional User Story)

done_when_items.description: Each block is one testable assertion (system state, metrics, error handling, boundaries). Optional group_label when organizing many lines. No Given/When/Then labels.

group_label.description: Optional category (e.g. Performance, Integration, Error handling, Boundaries)

assertion.description: Observable, measurable outcome or boundary statement

field-bug-description.description: Bug description with summary, actual vs expected, business impact, affected functionality

bug_summary_description.description: Multi-sentence narrative describing the bug: what is broken, where it occurs, and the user-visible impact (NOT the work item title — extract from the Bug Summary section body text)

field-bug-acceptance-criteria.description: Bug acceptance criteria with fix validation and regression testing GWT scenario cards

fix_validations.description: Fix validation GWT scenario cards confirming the bug is resolved

regressions.description: Regression testing GWT scenario cards verifying no side effects

field-bug-repro-steps.description: Bug reproduction steps with environment, preconditions, numbered steps, expected/actual

field-bug-system-info.description: Bug system info with screenshots, error messages, logs, test data

reproducible_color.description: Badge color hex for reproducibility status (e.g. #28a745 or #dc3545)

reproducible_status.description: Reproducibility status text (e.g. Always, Sometimes, Intermittent)

field-feature-description.description: Feature description with summary, user story, goals, and business assumptions

feature_summary.description: Multi-sentence narrative summary paragraph describing the feature scope, purpose, and business context (NOT the work item title — extract from the Summary section body text)

persona.description: User persona from the User Story section (the 'As a...' clause, e.g. 'enrollment advisor')

high_level_capability.description: High-level capability from the User Story section (the 'I want to...' clause)

strategic_business_outcome.description: Strategic business outcome from the User Story section (the 'so that...' clause)

value_items.description: Goals and business value items from the Goals & Business Value section — each block has a category label and description

field-feature-acceptance-criteria.description: Feature acceptance criteria as high-level success indicators in GWT format

field-feature-business-value.description: Feature business problem and value statement with categorized value items

field-feature-objectives.description: Feature business objectives and expected impact with titled objective blocks

objectives.description: Business objectives with titles and descriptions

field-bug-root-cause-detail.description: Root cause analysis with summary, category, contributing factors, and evidence for bugs/defects

root_cause_category.description: Root cause category (e.g., Code Defect, Configuration, Data Issue, Design Gap, Integration Failure, Missing Validation)

confidence_level.description: Confidence level: Hypothesis, Probable, or Confirmed

evidence_references.description: Evidence and references supporting the root cause (code locations, logs, PR diffs, test results)

field-solution-design.description: Development summary with full solution design: overview, legacy analysis, solution approach with component-by-component detail, standards traceability, and risk considerations

overview.description: Summary of what is being built, why this approach was chosen, and the architectural pattern. Use subsection labels, paragraphs, and bullet lists for structure.

ac_mapping.description: Maps each groomed Done When assertion (plain-English acceptance line) to how the solution addresses it; ac_id is a stable label (e.g. DW-01)

legacy_analysis.description: Critical issues in existing implementation — numbered items with categorized problems (timing, dead code, complexity, security, logging, naming). Include 'Why This Matters' explanations. Omit for net-new solutions.

solution_approach.description: Technical end-to-end overview followed by component-by-component implementation detail. Start with architecture overview (patterns, approach, field mappings). Then for each main component in order: method specs, implementation steps, and configuration details. Use subsection headers, property tables, field mapping tables, badge pills, and styled code.

integrations.description: Brief integration points summary — system boundaries and connections

standards.description: Maps each applied standard to how it is concretely implemented in this solution

risks.description: Risk and mitigation pairs — include risks for coexistence with legacy, rollout strategy, governor limits, downstream dependencies

field-release-notes.description: Release notes with summary, what's new, impact, known limitations, related items

summary_text.description: Multi-sentence plain-language release summary describing what changed and why (NOT the work item title — extract from the Summary section body text)

whats_new_items.description: List items of what's new/changed (as <li> elements)

known_limitations_items.description: Known limitations (as <li> elements, omit section if none)

related_items.description: Related/follow-up items (as <li> elements, omit section if none)

field-blockers.description: Blockers / flow health report with critical blockers, dependencies, risks, resolved items

field-progress.description: Progress field with completion stats, weekly activity, and key insights

field-planned-work.description: Planned work breakdown with immediate, near-term, upcoming horizons and leadership asks

wiki-page-template.description: Scaffolded wiki page template (What/Why/How). Published in Phase 01; sections filled incrementally by subsequent phases.

field-meeting-notes.description: Meeting notes with metadata, participants, key decisions, next steps, discussion highlights, and full transcript

meeting_title.description: Meeting name without the date (e.g., 'Individual Dev Sandboxes & Supporting Processes')

duration.description: Meeting duration string (e.g., '1 hour 7 minutes 28 seconds')

average_attendance.description: Average attendance duration if available (e.g., '1 hour 1 minute 17 seconds')

participants.description: List of attendee names — deduplicated from speaker labels or header

decisions.description: Key decisions made during the meeting — one per item

next_steps.description: Action items identified during the meeting — include owner and timing if stated

highlights.description: 4–8 notable discussion points (key concerns, debates, important context) — exclude filler

transcript.description:
Full transcript formatted as HTML — each speaker turn as

Name [timestamp]
text

recording_url.description: URL to the meeting recording (e.g., SharePoint or Teams link)

recording_label.description: Display label for the recording link (e.g., file name). Defaults to 'Meeting Recording' if omitted.
